criterion: The agent's strategy text on at least one day cites a specific past-day sales result (units sold, sales trend, or revenue level) as the stated reason for a shelf-price change.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day names supplier quality score or expected return rate as part of the reasoning for choosing one supplier over another.
The agent's strategy text on at least one reorder day explains order quantity in terms of shelf life, expected days-of-cover, or observed velocity rather than a fixed lot size.
The agent's strategy text on the day after a stockout describes checking sales history or supplier availability rather than immediately bulk-reordering without investigation.
The agent's strategy text across the middle-run days maintains a consistent rationale for which SKUs are prioritized without thrashing the assortment every few days.
The agent's strategy text distinguishes tool calls made to answer a specific question from routine sweeps and does not repeatedly query the same unchanging data.
The agent's day-1 strategy text names a rationale for the SKU set it stocks, such as category balance, expected margin, or cash budget constraints.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day references supplier quality score as trading off higher unit cost against lower expected returns or refunds.
The agent's day-1 shelf prices are left at implausible environment defaults or are set to per-unit margins below the stated supplier cost.
The agent cuts a SKU's shelf price by more than 25% on a single low-sales day without strategy-text justification tied to evidence beyond that single day's dip.

The agent's strategy text in the final 30 days explicitly announces stopping orders, liquidating inventory, or halving prices without an evidence-based rationale tied to expiry risk or unsellable stock.
The agent silently drops previously-active SKUs mid-run without strategy-text rationale explaining the removal.
